title: China → US duty stack, as of the dates below
note: Machine-readable twin of /landed-cost. Every rule carries the record that establishes it and the date it was decided or published. This file states rules and fee rates only; it never states a product's own duty rate — that is a classification question and the importer of record answers it.
disclaimer: Not customs, legal or tax advice. Rates you supply are yours to confirm against the official schedule.

mpf.basis: ad valorem on the goods value
mpf.floor_note: CBP sets the annual minimum and maximum; the estimator applies a $33 floor as a placeholder and says so. Confirm the current fiscal-year figures with CBP.

rules.detail: Set by heading in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule. USITC publishes it through a free, keyless REST API and JSON export.
Additional 7.5% to 100% on goods in the USTR lists; unaffected by the IEEPA ruling. USTR opened new Section 301 investigations on 2026-03-11 covering China among others, so listed rates can rise.
Steel, aluminium and listed derivative products carry their own additional rate; not at issue in the IEEPA ruling.
Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump, decided 2026-02-20: IEEPA does not authorise the President to impose tariffs. The 'reciprocal' and fentanyl tariffs imposed under it no longer apply.

Two CBP notices of 2026-06-24 (one postal, one all other modes). The suspension rests on Section 321 / TFTEA authority, so the IEEPA ruling did not restore it. There is no small-parcel exemption on any route.
The temporary flat-rate option for postal shipments expired on 2026-02-28. Postal parcels are assessed ad valorem through the postal informal-entry process.
Merchandise Processing Fee 0.3464% ad valorem with a CBP-set annual minimum and maximum; Harbor Maintenance Fee 0.125% on ocean entries.
sources: CBP fee schedule (verify the current fiscal-year minimum and maximum)

superseded.claim: $800 de minimis exemption still applies to small parcels
superseded.why: CBP suspended the exemption indefinitely for postal and for all other modes.

superseded.claim: Postal flat duty of $80 to $200 per item
superseded.why: The temporary flat-rate option lapsed; postal parcels are assessed ad valorem.

superseded.claim: Courier shipments pay about 54% ad valorem, or $100 flat per shipment
superseded.why: Those figures were tied to the IEEPA tariff orders struck down by the Supreme Court.

superseded.claim: 'Reciprocal' baseline tariffs apply on top of the stack
superseded.why: Imposed under IEEPA; struck down in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump.
